title: Ops Safety-net Activation Manifest and 90-day Tactical Checklist
summary: A pragmatic activation manifest and prioritized 90-day checklist to onboard services into the company-wide ops safety-net. Focus areas: minimal production signal guarantees, automated fallback patterns, SLO adoption runway, and lightweight runbook coverage for new and migrating model-serving endpoints.
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a tactical, cross-functional activation manifest intended for platform-engineering, serving-runtime, SRE, product-hosted-api, and solutions-eng. Goal is to provide an executable 90-day plan teams can adopt to bring any model-serving surface under the Ops Safety-net with minimal friction.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Increasing service diversity (hosted, dedicated, private) means inconsistent observability and fallbacks.
- Teams often ramp SLOs late in launch cycle; that creates risky launches and firefighting.
- We need a repeatable lightweight path that yields measurable reliability improvements without heavy ops burden.

Principles (how we operate):
- Minimum bar first: instrument a small, high-signal set (latency P99, user error rate, model-availability) before broad telemetry.
- Fast feedback: short canary windows and an automated rollback/fallback policy you can test in staging.
- Ownership clarity: every checklist item has an owner and a clear acceptance criterion.
- De-risk early: prioritize automated fallbacks over manual escalation.

Outcome metrics (team-level acceptance):
- Instrumentation coverage >= 3 core signals (95% of requests include trace id, latency histogram, error tag)
- Canary pass rate >= 98% across three consecutive runs before rollout
- Baseline SLO targets for first-release: availability >= 99.9% (non-degraded mode) and latency P99 <= 1.2x target SLA for customer tier (tier-specific override allowed)
- Runbook completeness: high-level runbook + 2 tested run-throughs with oncall in 30 days

90-day phased checklist (prioritized, week-grouped):
Phase 0: Pre-activation (week -1 to 0) - owner: service/product lead
- Confirm service boundary and critical routes (list routes + expected QPS)
- Identify downstream dependencies and any vendor-managed model endpoints
- Quick security checklist: encryption-at-rest, KMS usage validated
- Acceptance: kickoff note posted in #ops-activation Slack and linked to ticket

Phase 1: Minimal Signals + Canary Framework (weeks 1–3) - owner: telemetry engineer
Week 1:
- Add trace id header propagation and ensure traces surface in the tracing UI
- Emit latency histograms (buckets aligned with platform catalog) and a boolean tag for model-cache-hit
- Add a simple synthetic canary in staging that calls the primary flow every 5m
- Acceptance: dashboard shows fresh synthetic canary data and alerts configured for failure
Week 2–3:
- Wire platform-level canary orchestration to run against a subset of traffic (5–10%)
- Implement a lightweight anomaly detector (baseline + 3 sigma) for response size and latency
- Acceptance: canary automation can pause rollouts and send a structured incident alert

Phase 2: Automated Fallbacks & Degradation Policies (weeks 4–6) - owner: serving-runtime lead
- Implement two-tier fallback: model-variant degrade (lossy quantized variant) + local cached response fallback for critical routes
- Add circuit-breaker with exponential backoff counters exposed to metrics backend
- Acceptance: simulated model node failure triggers fallback chain in staging and metrics reflect transitions

Phase 3: SLOs, Error Budget & Ops Flow (weeks 7–10) - owner: SRE lead
- Define SLO(s) per route and map to customer-impact tiers; list measurement windows and burn policy
- Create error-budget policy: automated remediation triggers (scale-up, rollback) when burn > 30% in 1h
- Establish oncall playbook for SLO breaches including channels and async reporters
- Acceptance: SLO page created and linked, error-budget remediation exercised in tabletop

Phase 4: Harden, Test, and Launch (weeks 11–12) - owner: platform release manager
- Run full blast tests (capacity and latency tail cases) and verify autoscale policies and quota guards
- Schedule a controlled ramp with progressive traffic percentages (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and guardrails
- Conduct two runbook drills with SRE and service engineers (one simulating network partition, one model-corruption)
- Acceptance: post-ramp report showing SLO compliance and incident playbook signoff

Runbook/Playbook template (minimum deliverables):
- TL;DR (1 paragraph): what this service does and why it matters
- Primary contact and escalation path (name + pager/team)
- Owned SLOs and how they are measured (metric name, window, target)
- Known failure modes and graceful degradation steps
- Fallback policy matrix (when to switch model variant, when to serve cached content)
- Rollback and rollback pre-checks checklist
- Post-incident checklist and retrospective owner

Operational tooling and automation (quick wins):
- Use platform feature:canary-orchestrator to schedule synthetic canaries and automatic pause conditions (ENG-2145)
- Enable prefix/KV caching for route groups that show stable prefixes (reduces tail cost and improves P99)
- Add structured diagnostic payloads in traces to speed RCA (model id, quantization flag, gpu-metric snapshot)

Cross-team coordination and rituals:
- Weekly activation sync (30m) for active services during weeks 1–8: attendees: service lead, SRE, platform-engineer, telemetry rep, product manager
- Bi-weekly readiness gating review with platform release manager for ramp decisions
- Slack channel naming convention: #ops-activation/<service-name> with a pinned checklist and runbook link

Dependencies and blocking risks:
- Full metrics retention and storage quotas (finance/observability cost decision) - mitigation: short retention for high-cardinality signals until vetted
- Model-variant compatibility: not all models support lossy quantization; require research fallback options
- Capacity: Dedicated pools vs hosted capacity shifts can change latency profiles — schedule capacity reservation when ramping

Risk map and mitigation highlights:
- Risk: Late SLO definition causes noisy alerts post-launch. Mitigation: SRE-led template and gating before any >10% traffic ramp.
- Risk: Cascade failure from a third-party embed provider. Mitigation: contract fallback + circuit-breaker and synthetic probes.
- Risk: High observability cost from too many high-card signals. Mitigation: telemetry budget and sampling knobs in the SDK.

Measurement and reporting cadence:
- Weeklies: activation progress (OKRs: instrumentation coverage, canary success rate, runbook done)
- Post-ramp: 14-day monitoring window for aggravated regressions with automated rollback hotfix window
- Quarterly: reliability retrospective and dependent-entity scorecard (latency, availability, incident count)

Playbook handoff checklist (for when service is considered under the Ops Safety-net):
- Dashboard with SLO tiles live and alerted
- Runbook pinned and two drills completed
- Canary automation enabled with defined pass/fail thresholds
- Fallback chain verified in production-like staging
- SLO page created in central SLO registry and linked from the service README

Quick templates (copy/paste snippets):
- Canary alert rule: "canary.failure_rate > 2% over 5m for 3 runs"
- Circuit-breaker rule: "if consecutive 5m failures > 200 then open for 10m and scale-up"

Next immediate actions (this week):
- Platform-engineering: provision short-lived canary cluster for new services (owner: Marina)
- SRE: publish SLO template and schedule tabletop for April 21 (owner: Priya)
- Telemetry: snapshot existing routes and spike synthetic coverage for top-5 routes (owner: Ethan)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is deliberately prescriptive at the tactical level. Feedback welcome on thresholds and the right balance between automation and human-in-the-loop.
- We should pilot with two services (one hosted api, one dedicated pool) to validate assumptions about fallback latencies and error-budget triggers.

Appendix: short glossary
- Canary orchestration: automated incremental traffic routing with automated pause/rollback triggers
- Error budget: permissible SLO burn used to trigger remediation actions
- Fallback chain: ordered set of responses (model-variant, cached response, explanatory error) used to maintain availability

End of document.
